name: tree-view
title: Tree view
summary: A hierarchy of items that open and close: rows that begin further in at each level, a chevron at the start or the end of every row that holds others — or none, the folder glyph opening — an optional glyph, a name on one line, a note below it or beside it and a short value; read and opened only, or with one item or several chosen by the quiet selection, names edited in place and new items named in a row of their own where the product asks; the rows of the open parents above what is shown pinned at the top while it scrolls; moved through with the arrow keys as one stop in the focus order; with room for touch or drawn closer for a tool and for a small tree inside text.

anatomy.description: The column that holds the rows, named by its label. It draws no fill, no edge and no space of its own, and does not scroll. One stop in the focus order.
One thing in the hierarchy (an item of the item kind): its row and, while it is a parent and open, the rows of the items it holds, which begin one level further in.

An item's row: the box that carries hover, focus and press and the selected fill. With highlight indented it begins further from the start edge for each level; with highlight full it spans the tree's width. It ends at the tree's end edge; the hit area is the tree's whole width.

The mark of a parent's open and closed, where chevron says: at the start of the row (the icon set's chevron_right, pointing toward the end of the line while closed and turned a quarter turn to point down while open) or at its very end, after the trailing content (the icon set's expand_more, turned a half turn while open, as the navigation drawer's and the accordion's). A leaf keeps the box empty, so that the names (or the values) of one level stand in one column. None where chevron is none, or where the tree is not expandable. Hidden from assistive technology, which is given the state in words.

A glyph of the system's icon set before the label, by name: what kind of thing the item is (a folder, a file, a group); a parent may name a second glyph for while it is open (folder_open beside folder). Where no icon is named, its room is kept while another item of the level has one (iconSpace). The product's choice; decorative.
The item's name and its accessible name. One line, cut with an ellipsis where it does not fit (the whole name in a tooltip); with labelWrap it wraps instead and is never cut.

A few words about the item: below the label (supportingPosition below, the default) or after it on its line (inline), quieter than the label. One line, cut with an ellipsis; with supportingWrap it wraps instead.
The trailing slot's content at the end of the row: a tag, a swatch, a mark that the item changed. Not interactive; part of the row.
A short value at the end of the row, after the trailing content: a count, a size, the present value. One line.
A hairline down from an open parent beside the rows it holds, under the parent's first leading mark, where guides says: always, or while the pointer is over the tree or focus is in it. Decorative.
A row one level further in under an open parent that is fetching what it holds: a loading indicator and the words the product gives. Not an item: it takes no focus and cannot be chosen.

The whole of a name or a note that is cut (TRV-50): a plain tooltip with the label, or a rich one with the label as its title and the supporting text, beside the row on hover and on keyboard focus. Only while something is cut.

The row of an open parent above the rows that are shown, held at the top of the scrolling box while what it holds scrolls under it (stickyParents): the same row, with an opaque fill and a hairline under the last one (TRV-53).

While an item's name is being edited, or a new item named: an Embedded text input on one line in the place of the label and the supporting text, inside a box the tree draws with the focus indicator around it. The rest of the row stays as it was.

A row the tree adds for the time a new item is being named: at the level of the selected item, after its rows, with a closed chevron for a parent, the glyph the product names and the edit field. Not an item: it is gone when the name is given or given up.
Gap-then-ring indicator shown for keyboard focus of an item, drawn inside its row's container.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the tree: what the hierarchy is ("Project files", "Every token"). Required: a tree is one stop in the focus order and is announced by this name.

props.name: selection
props.description: Whether people choose items. none: a tree that is read and opened — a figure of a file system in a page, a structure to look through; its leaves answer nothing and its parents open and close. single: one item is chosen (the file shown in the pane beside the tree, the token being edited). multiple: any number are chosen, each by itself. An item is chosen by its value; an item without one cannot be chosen.

props.name: value
props.description: The value of the selected item while selection is single; null selects none. The tree sets it when an item is chosen and emits change; the product may also set it.

props.name: values
props.description: The values of the selected items while selection is multiple: a list of strings (the platforms take a set). An empty list selects none.

props.name: density
props.description: How much room a row takes, in a table's and an accordion's words: the row's least height, its paddings and its glyphs' size, and never the gap between the icon and the label (iconGap). regular (a 48 row with a 14 label in the default system, a navigation drawer's row) is the tree of a product used by touch as well as by pointer. compact (a 32 row with a 13 label, a table's compact row) is for a tool used with a pointer, where hundreds of rows are looked through, and for a small tree inside a page of text. For touch a row is never lower than the touch target in either. A design system may add values.

props.name: chevron
props.description: Where a parent's chevron stands. start: at the start of its row, before the icon (a file tree, the tree pattern). end: at the very end of the row, after the trailing content and the trailing text (a settings tree, the navigation drawer's place). none: no chevron; a parent that names an icon and an open icon shows open and closed by its glyph, which a press opens and closes, and the arrow keys always open and close (TRV-44).

props.name: expandable
props.description: Whether parents open and close at all. false: every parent is shown open, no chevron is drawn, nothing toggles, and no row is exposed as expanded or collapsed — a structure that is always shown whole (an outline, a table of contents of a document). An item's own expandable is read only while this is true.

props.name: guides
props.description: Hairlines down from each open parent beside the rows it holds, for a deep tree where the indent alone no longer shows which rows belong together. none: no lines. shown: always. hover: while a pointer is over the tree or keyboard focus is in it, faded in and out. Decorative. On the web the bare attribute, and true, are shown.

props.name: indent
props.description: How far each level begins further in than the one above it. null (auto, the default): a child's start stands where its parent's label begins, so the step follows what the parent's row holds before its label — the chevron at the start, the icon or the icon's room. A number: that many points (px, dp), the product's explicit choice; 0 sets no level in, and then no guide is drawn. A design system sets what auto rests on through the parts' tokens and the level's indent token.

props.name: iconSpace
props.description: Whether a row without an icon keeps the icon's room, so that the labels of a level stand in one column. auto: it does while another item of the same level has an icon. always: every row keeps it. never: only a row with an icon has the room.

props.name: iconGap
props.description: The room between the icon (or its kept room) and the label, in points. null (auto): comp.tree-view.icon.gap, which no density changes. A number is the product's explicit choice.

props.name: highlight
props.description: How far a row's fill reaches — the selected fill and the hover and press layers, and the focus ring with them. indented: from where the row's level begins to the tree's end edge, so that the fill shows the level. full: from the tree's start edge to its end edge, as file browsers draw it. The hit area is the whole width either way.

props.name: labelWrap
props.description: false: a label is one line, cut with an ellipsis where it does not fit, and the whole of it is shown in a tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus while it is cut. true: it wraps onto as many lines as it needs and is never cut. The accessible name is the whole label either way.

props.name: supportingWrap
props.description: As labelWrap, for the supporting text: one line cut with an ellipsis (the whole in the tooltip), or wrapping. A supporting text beside the label (inline) shares the label's line and follows labelWrap.

props.name: stickyParents
props.description: Keeps the rows of the open parents that the rows at the top of the scrolling box belong to pinned at its top while what they hold scrolls under them, as an editor's sticky scroll does, so that a person deep in a long tree sees where they are. The pinned rows are the rows themselves and work as they do. On by default in the tree view (off in the navigation drawer, which is short). A tree in no scrolling box pins nothing.

props.name: stickyMax
props.description: The most rows pinned at once, one per level; where more parents are above what is shown, the innermost of them are the ones pinned. 0 pins none.

props.name: editable
props.description: Lets people rename items in place: a double-click on a row's label, or F2 on a focused row, puts the label into a text field; Enter or leaving the field gives the new name, Escape gives it up. The tree changes no label itself: it emits the item's rename and the product sets the label. New items are named the same way whatever this says, in a row the product asks for (TRV-48).

props.name: editLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the field in which a name is edited or a new item named ("Name"). Tanrei ships no words of its own. Required where editable is true or a new item may be asked for.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: The words of a loading row ("Loading…"), drawn beside its loading indicator and used as the indicator's name. Tanrei ships no words of its own. Required where any item may be loading.

items.name: item
items.summary: One thing in the hierarchy: a row with a label and, where it holds other items, a chevron that opens and closes them. An item that holds items, or says it will, is a parent; every other item is a leaf. The fixture's content is unused.

props.name: value
props.description: What identifies the item: the tree's value (single) or values (multiple) select the item whose value they hold, and change carries it. Unique within the tree. Empty, the item cannot be chosen: a press on its row opens or closes it where it is a parent and does nothing where it is a leaf.

props.name: label
props.description: Its name, drawn in its row and used as its accessible name. Plain text; the label slot takes its place where the product needs inline content. Required unless the label slot is filled.

props.name: supportingText
props.description: A few words about the item ("the source of truth, edited by hand"), drawn below the label or beside it as supportingPosition says, and read as the item's description. Empty draws the label alone.

props.name: supportingPosition
props.description: Where the supporting text stands: below the label, on a line of its own (the default), or inline, after the label on the label's line.

props.name: trailingText
props.description: A short value at the end of the row: a count, a size, the present value. One line; read after the supporting text as the item's description.

props.name: icon
props.description: The name of a glyph in the system's icon set, drawn before the label: what kind of thing the item is. The tree has no glyphs of its own for a folder or a file: the product names them. Decorative.

props.name: openIcon
props.description: The name of a second glyph, drawn in the icon's place while the parent is open (folder_open beside folder). Ignored on a leaf and while icon is empty. Where the tree's chevron is none, the two glyphs are what shows open and closed, and the glyph is what a press opens and closes. Decorative.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the items a parent holds are shown under its row. Set by the product for a parent that starts open; the web sets it itself when the user opens or closes the parent, and a controlled platform leaves it to the caller. Ignored on a leaf.

props.name: expandable
props.description: Says that the item holds items the product has not given yet: it is drawn and exposed as a parent, with a chevron, and its toggle tells the product to give them. An item that holds items is a parent whatever this says. Read only while the tree's expandable is true.

props.name: loading
props.description: Says that the product is fetching what the item holds: while the item is open a loading row is drawn under it, after any items it already holds, and the item is exposed as busy. Ignored on a leaf.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Makes it unavailable: it keeps its place and its open, draws its disabled look, and cannot be chosen, opened or closed by the user. The arrow keys still reach it, and the items it shows keep their own disabled.

slots.name: label
slots.description: The product's own label content in place of the label prop: text with inline content (a code span, a part of the name marked as a match). The tree draws it in the label's style and color. No control.

slots.name: trailing
slots.description: Content at the end of the row, before the trailing text and before an end chevron: a tag, a swatch, a mark. The tree places it and gives it no style. No control; it is part of the row and is read as part of the item's description where it has text.

events.name: toggle
events.description: The parent opened or closed: by the user from its chevron, its row or the keyboard, or by the platform's search finding text under it; carries its new open state. Emitted exactly once per change, when the change begins. The moment to give the items of a parent that is expandable.

events.name: rename
events.description: The user gave the item a new name in place (TRV-46): carries the new label — not empty, with no white space at its ends, and not the label it had — and the label it had. Emitted exactly once per name given. The tree draws the label it had until the product sets the new one; a product that refuses the name leaves the label as it is.

events.name: change
events.description: The user changed the selection — by a press, a key, a range or select-all; carries value (single) or values (multiple) after the change, once per gesture.

events.name: create
events.description: The user named the new item in the row the product asked for (TRV-48): carries its label (not empty, with no white space at its ends), whether it is a parent or a leaf, the item it goes under (none for the first level) and the item it follows (none where it is the first). Emitted exactly once; the tree takes its own row away as it emits it, and the product adds the item.

behavior.text: THE tree view SHALL lay out the rows of its items in one column, in the order given and depth first: an item's row and then, WHILE the item is a parent and open, the rows of the items it holds, before the row of the item that follows it. It SHALL be as wide as the layout it is placed in gives it, with its start edge on the start edge of what is around it; SHALL bring no outer space, no fill and no edge of its own (PRS-15: the space between it and its neighbours is its container's); SHALL have no minimum width, no maximum width and no height of its own; and SHALL NOT scroll: it is as tall as the rows it shows, and the product places a long tree in a scrolling box of its own, at whose top the rows of the open parents above what is shown are pinned (TRV-53). Rows SHALL touch: there is no space and no line between two rows.

THE tree view SHALL draw each item's row as a container at least as high as its density gives (comp.tree-view.container.height.regular for regular and comp.tree-view.container.height.compact for compact) and growing with its text, with corners comp.tree-view.container.shape, padded at its start and end by comp.tree-view.container.padding-inline.regular for regular and comp.tree-view.container.padding-inline.compact for compact and above its first line and below its last by comp.tree-view.container.padding-block.regular for regular and comp.tree-view.container.padding-block.compact for compact. Inside it SHALL lay out, from the start: the chevron's box WHILE chevron is start (TRV-4); the icon, or its kept room (TRV-5, TRV-43); the text, which takes the remaining width and holds the label and the supporting text (TRV-6, TRV-7); the trailing slot's content, where there is any; the trailing text, where the item has one (TRV-7); and the chevron's box WHILE chevron is end (TRV-4). Between the icon (or its room) and the text it SHALL keep iconGap — comp.tree-view.icon.gap while iconGap is null, the same in every density — and between each other two of them comp.tree-view.container.gap.regular for regular and comp.tree-view.container.gap.compact for compact. THE tree view SHALL centre the chevron, the icon, the trailing content and the trailing text on the label's first line and keep them there however tall the text grows, and any height a row has beyond its text SHALL be shared equally above and below it.
behavior.verify: Under the default system: a regular row of one line is 48 high, its chevron box 20 at 12 from its container's start, its icon 20 at 44, its label at 76 (icon gap 12); in the compact density the chevron box and the icon are 16 and the label begins 8 + 16 + 8 + 16 + 12 = 60 in, the icon gap the same 12. With chevron end the chevron box is the last thing in the row, a gap after the trailing text.

behavior.text: THE tree view SHALL show an item's depth by where its row's content begins: the content of an item of the first level SHALL begin where the tree's start edge and its padding put it, and the content of every deeper item SHALL begin one step further from that edge than its parent's. WHILE indent is null (auto) the step SHALL be the length from the parent's content start to where the parent's label begins — the chevron's box and a gap WHILE chevron is start and the tree is expandable, plus the icon's box (or its kept room, TRV-43) and iconGap WHERE the parent's row has an icon or keeps its room — so that a child's start stands where its parent's label begins, and comp.tree-view.level.indent.regular for regular and comp.tree-view.level.indent.compact for compact where the parent's row holds nothing before its label; WHILE indent is a number the step SHALL be that number of points, and 0 SHALL set no level in. WHILE highlight is indented the row's container (its fill, its state layer and its focus indicator) SHALL begin where its content's level begins, its padding before the content; WHILE highlight is full every container SHALL begin at the tree's start edge (TRV-51). Every container SHALL end at the tree's end edge. WHILE the steps of an item's levels would begin its label past half of the tree's width THE tree view SHALL begin that row no further in than puts its label at half of the width, so that a deep tree in a narrow window keeps half of its width for names, SHALL still expose the item's true level (TRV-32), and in debug builds SHALL report the depth once.
behavior.verify: The fixture basic (no icons, chevron start) under the default system: levels one to three begin their content at 12, 44 and 76 — each child's chevron where its parent's label begins. The fixture icons: 12, 76, 140. The fixture indent-16: 12, 28, 44. The fixture indent-0: every level at 12, and no guide. The fixture deep in a stage 320 wide: no row's label begins past 160.

behavior.text: WHILE the tree is expandable and chevron is start or end THE tree view SHALL keep a box of comp.tree-view.chevron.size.regular for regular and comp.tree-view.chevron.size.compact for compact in every row, at its start WHILE chevron is start and at its very end — after the trailing content and the trailing text — WHILE chevron is end. In the row of a parent — an item that holds items, or whose expandable is true — it SHALL draw in that box, in the chevron color of the item's condition (comp.tree-view.unselected.chevron.color, comp.tree-view.selected.chevron.color), with sys.icon.family.unselected and sys.icon.fill.unselected, sys.icon.weight and an optical size clamped between sys.icon.optical-size.min and sys.icon.optical-size.max: at the start, the glyph chevron_right as the icon helper draws it WHILE the parent is closed, pointing toward the end of the line, turned a quarter turn to point down WHILE it is open; at the end, the glyph expand_more WHILE closed, turned a half turn WHILE open. In the row of a leaf it SHALL draw nothing in the box and keep the box, so that the labels (at the start) or the trailing texts (at the end) of one level stand in one column. WHILE chevron is none, or the tree is not expandable, THE tree view SHALL keep no chevron's box. The chevron, and the icon of an item that names an open icon (TRV-5), SHALL be the only things about a row that show whether its item is open: the container, the label and the texts SHALL be the same open and closed. THE tree view SHALL keep the chevron from assistive technology, which is given the state in words (TRV-32), and a disabled parent SHALL keep its chevron.
behavior.verify: The fixture basic: the open parents' chevrons point down, the closed parent's points right, and the leaves' labels begin on the line of the labels of the parents beside them. The fixture chevron-end: every chevron is the last thing of its row, a gap after its trailing text, expand_more closed and turned a half turn open. The fixture chevron-none: no row keeps a chevron's box.

behavior.text: WHILE an item's icon is not empty THE tree view SHALL draw that glyph of the system's icon set after the chevron's box (or first, where there is none), in a box of comp.tree-view.icon.size.regular for regular and comp.tree-view.icon.size.compact for compact, in the icon color of the item's condition (comp.tree-view.unselected.icon.color, comp.tree-view.selected.icon.color), with the family and fill of that condition (sys.icon.family.selected and sys.icon.fill.selected for a selected item, sys.icon.family.unselected and sys.icon.fill.unselected otherwise), sys.icon.weight and an optical size clamped between sys.icon.optical-size.min and sys.icon.optical-size.max, and SHALL keep it from assistive technology. WHILE icon is empty THE tree view SHALL draw no glyph and keep its room as TRV-43 says. THE tree view SHALL have no glyph of its own for any kind of item. WHILE an item is a parent, is open and its openIcon is not empty THE tree view SHALL draw the openIcon glyph instead of icon, in the same place, box, color, family and fill, and SHALL draw icon again WHEN the parent closes; the glyph SHALL change at once, WHEN the change of open begins, with no motion of its own. THE tree view SHALL ignore openIcon on a leaf and WHILE icon is empty, and SHALL draw icon alone WHILE openIcon is empty.
behavior.verify: The fixture chevron-none: the open parents draw folder_open and the closed parent folder; opening the closed parent draws folder_open at once, and closing it draws folder again. The fixture icons, which names no open icon: every parent draws folder open and closed.

behavior.text: THE tree view SHALL draw an item's label in the text style of its density (comp.tree-view.label.typescale.regular for regular and comp.tree-view.label.typescale.compact for compact) and the label color of its condition (comp.tree-view.unselected.label.color, comp.tree-view.selected.label.color). WHILE labelWrap is false the label SHALL be one line, cut at the end of its own direction with an ellipsis where it does not fit, and shown whole in the tooltip of TRV-50 while it is cut; WHILE labelWrap is true it SHALL wrap and SHALL never be cut, and a name with no place to break (a path, an identifier) SHALL break where it must rather than widen the tree. The accessible name SHALL be the whole label either way. WHERE the item's label slot holds content THE tree view SHALL draw that content in the label's place, size and color instead of the label, on one line or wrapping as labelWrap says, and SHALL leave a code span in it its own typeface. The label slot and the trailing slot SHALL hold no control: IF either holds a link, a button or a field THE tree view SHALL still render it and in debug builds report that a row holds no control; a platform that cannot inspect its slot content SHALL state the rule in its README and docs page.
behavior.verify: The fixture long-labels (labelWrap false) in a stage 400 wide: each long label is one line ending in an ellipsis, and its accessible name is the whole label. The fixture long-labels-wrap: the labels wrap and are never cut.

behavior.text: WHILE an item's supportingText is not empty THE tree view SHALL draw it in comp.tree-view.supporting-text.typescale and the supporting-text color of the item's condition (comp.tree-view.unselected.supporting-text.color, comp.tree-view.selected.supporting-text.color): WHILE supportingPosition is below, on a line of its own under the label, starting where the label starts — one line cut with an ellipsis (the whole in the tooltip of TRV-50) WHILE supportingWrap is false, wrapping and never cut WHILE it is true; WHILE supportingPosition is inline, after the label in the same block of text and comp.tree-view.container.gap.regular for regular and comp.tree-view.container.gap.compact for compact after the label's last word, on the label's baseline, sharing the label's line and its cut (TRV-6). WHILE an item's trailingText is not empty THE tree view SHALL draw it on one line, in comp.tree-view.trailing-text.typescale and the trailing-text color of the item's condition (comp.tree-view.unselected.trailing-text.color, comp.tree-view.selected.trailing-text.color), after the trailing slot's content and before an end chevron; it SHALL NOT wrap, and WHILE it would take more than half of the row's inner width it SHALL be cut at the end of its own direction with an ellipsis, so that the label always keeps at least half. THE tree view SHALL give the trailing slot's content no style, and SHALL apply a disabled item's opacity to it with the rest of the row.
behavior.verify: The fixture supporting-text: each note stands below its label, one line. The fixture supporting-inline: each note follows its label on its line, a gap after it. The fixture trailing-text: the values stand at the row's end on the label's first line.

behavior.text: WHILE guides is shown or hover, and the step of a level is not 0 (TRV-3), THE tree view SHALL draw, for each open parent that shows at least one row under it, one line comp.tree-view.guide.width wide in comp.tree-view.guide.color, from the lower edge of the parent's row to the lower edge of the last row shown under it (the rows of its open descendants and a loading row included), centred under the parent's first leading thing: its chevron WHILE chevron is start; else its icon, where it has one; else the start of its label. The line SHALL lie in the indent of the rows it runs beside, SHALL keep its color and its full opacity in every state and condition of the rows beside it (a disabled item's opacity does not reach it), SHALL grow and shrink with the rows it runs beside as they are revealed and hidden (TRV-11), SHALL pass under a pinned row (TRV-53), SHALL be hidden from assistive technology, and SHALL take no space: a tree is laid out the same with and without guides. WHILE guides is hover THE tree view SHALL draw the lines WHILE a pointer is anywhere over the tree or keyboard focus is in it, and not otherwise, fading them in and out over comp.tree-view.motion.state-duration with comp.tree-view.motion.state-easing, at once where motion is reduced. WHILE guides is none THE tree view SHALL draw no line.
behavior.verify: The fixtures guides and compact-guides: one line under each open parent's chevron, none under a closed parent or a leaf; each fixture measures the same as its form without guides. The fixture chevron-none (guides shown): each line stands under its parent's icon; in the fixture guides-label (chevron none, no icons) under its parent's label start. The fixture indent-0 draws none. Test guides hover: no line until the pointer enters the tree or focus comes into it.

behavior.text: THE tree view SHALL draw a parent's open as the state of that parent alone: WHILE open is true the rows of the items it holds are shown under its row, and WHILE open is false they are not drawn, take no space, cannot take focus and are not exposed to assistive technology, whatever their own open says; a closed parent SHALL keep its descendants' open, so that it opens again as it was. WHEN the tree first appears it SHALL draw every parent as its open says, in its first frame, without the motion of TRV-11 and without emitting toggle. THE tree view SHALL ignore the open of a leaf. On a platform that keeps what it does not draw (the web, where the items stay in the document) THE tree view SHALL NOT remove or rebuild a closed parent's items.

WHEN the user presses the chevron of a parent that is not disabled, by pointer or touch, THE tree view SHALL emit that item's toggle exactly once with its new open state, SHALL NOT change the selection, and on the web SHALL set the item's open itself (a controlled platform leaves it to the caller). WHEN the user presses the row of a parent that cannot be chosen (TRV-15) anywhere, or presses Enter or Space while focus is on it, THE tree view SHALL do the same: a row that has nothing to choose opens and closes. WHEN the user presses the row of an item that can be chosen outside its chevron THE tree view SHALL change the selection (TRV-16, TRV-17) and SHALL NOT open or close it: the chevron opens and the row chooses, and one press never does both. WHILE chevron is none the press rules of TRV-44 SHALL apply in place of this one. THE tree view SHALL NOT open a parent because the pointer rests on it, and SHALL NOT open or close anything for a second press that follows the first quickly: each press is answered by itself.
behavior.verify: Test in the fixture studio-tokens (selection single; the tiers and groups have no value): a press anywhere on a group's row emits one toggle and no change. In the fixture single (every item has a value): a press on a parent's label emits one change and no toggle; a press on its chevron emits one toggle and no change.

behavior.text: WHEN a parent's open changes THE tree view SHALL reveal or hide the rows under it from its row downward, the rows after them moving with their lower edge, and SHALL turn its chevron (a quarter turn at the start, a half turn at the end), over comp.tree-view.motion.disclosure-duration with comp.tree-view.motion.disclosure-easing, at once where motion is reduced. The rows SHALL be laid out once, at the size they have when shown, and the motion SHALL only change how much of them is seen: no label SHALL wrap again and nothing SHALL be measured again from frame to frame. Rows that are being hidden SHALL stay drawn until the motion ends and SHALL leave the arrow keys and assistive technology when it begins. WHEN open changes again before the motion ends THE tree view SHALL go on from where the motion is toward the new state, without a jump. toggle SHALL be emitted when the change begins, not when the motion ends.
behavior.verify: Test with the web's animations inspected: one height motion and one rotation of the chosen duration per change; none while prefers-reduced-motion is reduce. A navigation drawer's group, an accordion's item and a parent of the tree open over the same duration with the same curve in the default system.

behavior.text: WHEN a parent opens or closes THE tree view SHALL keep that parent's row where it is in the view, as far as the scrolling of what holds the tree allows, and move only what follows it; it SHALL NOT scroll for any other reason of its own, and the rows of a parent that opens MAY reach below the view's edge. WHEN a parent closes, or its items are taken away, while keyboard focus is on a row under it THE tree view SHALL move focus to that parent's row; WHEN the item that has focus is removed and no parent of it closed THE tree view SHALL move focus to the row that follows it or, where none does, the row before it. WHEN keyboard focus moves to a row that is not wholly in view — or lies under the pinned rows of TRV-53 — THE tree view SHALL have the scrolling box that holds it bring that row into view, below the pinned rows, by the least distance that shows it whole.

WHILE a parent is open and its loading is true THE tree view SHALL draw one loading row under it, after the rows of any items it already holds and one level further in than its own row: a container of that level and of the tree's density (TRV-2, TRV-3) holding, at the start of its content, a Loading indicator component of the small size named by loadingLabel, which the tree lays out and does not restyle, and after it loadingLabel in comp.tree-view.supporting-text.typescale and comp.tree-view.unselected.supporting-text.color. The loading row is not an item: it SHALL take no focus, answer no pointer and no key, SHALL NOT be counted among its parent's items, and SHALL be shown and hidden by the motion of TRV-11 with the rows beside it. THE tree view SHALL expose the parent as busy WHILE its loading is true, open or closed, and SHALL announce nothing itself when loading begins or ends. THE tree view SHALL fetch nothing: a parent whose expandable is true and that holds no items opens onto no rows, or onto the loading row, and what it holds is the product's to give, which it learns from toggle. WHILE an item may be loading and loadingLabel is empty THE tree view SHALL still draw the indicator, and in debug builds report that it has no name.
behavior.verify: The fixture loading: the open parent "packages" shows one loading row at the second level with the small indicator under the place of a child's chevron; the closed parent "apps" is expandable, shows a chevron and no row.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform can search the text of what is shown and reports a match that lies in rows it does not draw (on the web, the browser's find-in-page), WHEN the match is under a closed parent THE tree view SHALL open that parent and every closed parent above it, at once and without the motion of TRV-11, SHALL emit each one's toggle exactly once with true, and SHALL leave bringing the match into view to the platform; it SHALL do so for a disabled parent too, whose rows are still part of the page. On a platform that has no such search or cannot report such a match THE tree view SHALL NOT open anything for it.
behavior.verify: On the web, in a browser whose find-in-page reveals content hidden until found: searching for a name that only a closed parent holds opens it and marks the name, and one toggle with true was emitted.

behavior.text: THE tree view SHALL let an item be chosen exactly WHILE selection is single or multiple, the item's value is not empty and its disabled is false, a parent and a leaf alike. It SHALL render an item as selected, from the selected condition (comp.tree-view.selected.container.color and the selected tokens TRV-4 to TRV-7 name), WHILE selection is single and value equals the item's value, or selection is multiple and values holds it, and every other item from the unselected condition (comp.tree-view.unselected.container.color and the unselected tokens). WHEN value or values names no item THE tree view SHALL select nothing for that name, and WHEN two items carry the same value it SHALL still render them, both selected where that value is; in debug builds it SHALL report each of these. The selected fill SHALL be drawn on the item's own row and on no other: THE tree view SHALL NOT mark a parent because an item under it is selected, and SHALL NOT open a closed parent to show a selection; opening the parents of the item it selects is the product's, which knows the path. WHEN the tree first appears it SHALL draw every item in the condition value and values give it, in its first frame and without the motion of TRV-31: appearing is no change of selection.
behavior.verify: The fixtures single and multiple: the selected rows carry the selected fill (comp.tree-view.selected.container.color) from where their own level begins to the tree's end edge, and no other row differs from its unselected look. Each fixture that selects something, inserted into a page that is already drawn (and once with its layout read in the task that inserts it): its first frame is the state it rests in, every selected row already in the selected condition.

behavior.text: WHEN the user activates — by a press on its row outside the chevron, or by Enter or Space while focus is on it — an item that can be chosen in a tree whose selection is single and whose value is not that item's value THE tree view SHALL set value to the item's value, so that the item that was selected becomes unselected, and emit change exactly once; WHEN the item is already selected THE tree view SHALL change nothing and SHALL NOT emit change, because a single choice is never cleared by its own item.

WHEN the user activates — by a press on its row outside the chevron, with no modifier or with Ctrl (Command on Apple platforms), or by Space or Enter while focus is on it — an item that can be chosen in a tree whose selection is multiple THE tree view SHALL add the item's value to values, or remove it when values holds it, make that item the anchor of TRV-52, and emit change exactly once. Each item SHALL be chosen by itself: choosing a parent SHALL NOT choose the items it holds, a parent SHALL NOT show a mixed state for them, and closing a parent SHALL NOT change values.

WHILE selection is none THE tree view SHALL render every item from the unselected condition, SHALL ignore value and values, and SHALL expose no selected state. A leaf — and, in a tree whose selection is single or multiple, a leaf that cannot be chosen — SHALL then answer nothing: THE tree view SHALL draw no hover and no press answer on its row, SHALL emit nothing for a press on it, and SHALL still let the arrow keys reach it and show its keyboard focus (TRV-24, TRV-25), so that a person who reads the tree with a keyboard or a screen reader meets every row. A parent SHALL answer hover, focus and press on its whole row, which opens and closes it (TRV-10).
behavior.verify: The fixture file-tree: hovering "tanrei.resolver.json" changes nothing; hovering "tokens/" draws the hover layer on its row; Down from "tokens/" moves the focus ring through every row under it.

behavior.text: THE tree view SHALL be one stop in the focus order however many items it shows: Tab SHALL move focus into it to one row — the row that had focus last, or else the first selected item that is shown, or else the first row — and Tab again SHALL leave it; no other row, and nothing inside a row, SHALL be a stop. Focus that enters the tree SHALL NOT change the selection and SHALL NOT open or close anything. WHILE the tree shows no row it SHALL NOT be a stop.

WHEN focus is on a row and the user presses Down Arrow or Up Arrow THE tree view SHALL move focus to the next or the previous row that is shown, in the order the rows are drawn, whatever its level and whether or not it is disabled, without wrapping at the first and the last; WHEN the user presses Home or End it SHALL move focus to the first or the last row that is shown. It SHALL open and close nothing for these keys and SHALL NOT change the selection: selection does not follow focus. THE tree view SHALL NOT take these keys from the platform WHILE focus is not on one of its rows.

WHEN focus is on a row and the user presses the arrow key toward the end of the line (Right in a left-to-right layout) THE tree view SHALL act by the row it is on — whatever chevron says, so that a tree with no chevron still opens by the keyboard (TRV-44); WHILE the tree is not expandable every parent counts as open and nothing opens or closes (TRV-49): on a closed parent that is not disabled, open it as TRV-10 says and keep focus on it; on an open parent that shows at least one item, move focus to the first of them; on a leaf, on a disabled closed parent and on an open parent that shows none, do nothing. WHEN the user presses the arrow key toward the start of the line it SHALL likewise act by the row: on an open parent that is not disabled, close it as TRV-10 says and keep focus on it; on any other row that has a parent, move focus to that parent's row; on a row of the first level, do nothing.
behavior.verify: Test in the fixture basic: Right on a closed parent emits one toggle and focus stays; Right again moves to its first child; Left there returns to the parent; Left again closes it with one toggle. In a right-to-left layout Left opens and steps in, and Right closes and steps out.

behavior.text: WHEN focus is on a row and the user presses Enter or Space THE tree view SHALL do what a press on that row outside its chevron does: choose the item where it can be chosen (TRV-16, TRV-17), open or close it where it is a parent that cannot be chosen (TRV-10), and nothing on a leaf that cannot be chosen or on a disabled item. WHEN the user presses the asterisk key THE tree view SHALL open every closed parent that is not disabled among the focused row's siblings, itself included, emitting each one's toggle exactly once with true, and SHALL keep focus where it is. THE tree view SHALL leave every key it does not name here or in TRV-20, TRV-21, TRV-23, TRV-45 and TRV-52, and every key pressed with a modifier that those rules do not name, to the platform; WHILE an edit field is open (TRV-46) every key typed in it SHALL be the field's.

WHEN the user types printable characters while focus is on a row THE tree view SHALL move focus to the next row that is shown, after the focused one and going on from the first row after the last, whose label begins with the characters typed within one second of each other, compared without regard to case as the platform's locale does; one character typed again SHALL go on to the next such row; IF no label matches THE tree view SHALL keep focus where it is. It SHALL NOT open a closed parent to find a match, SHALL NOT change the selection, and SHALL NOT take a space typed inside such a run as an activation.

WHILE a row is hovered, keyboard-focused or pressed THE tree view SHALL render its container, label, supporting text, trailing text, icon, chevron and opacity from the component tokens of its condition in the highest-precedence active state, with precedence pressed over focused over hovered; focus gained by pointer or touch SHALL NOT select the focused state. Hover and press over any part of the row's hit area (TRV-26) SHALL answer on the whole container, as far as highlight says (TRV-51), the chevron's included; a row that answers nothing (TRV-18) SHALL take the focused state alone. The guide lines and the rows beside it SHALL NOT change under a pointer, a press or focus.
behavior.verify: Test under the `acme` fixture system, which values hovered, focused and pressed differently.

behavior.text: WHEN a row receives keyboard focus THE tree view SHALL show the focus ring inside the row's container — indented or full as highlight says (TRV-51) — following comp.tree-view.container.shape, so that neither a neighbouring row nor a scrolling ancestor cuts it, without animation, and at full strength on a disabled row too (TRV-27); focus gained by pointer or touch SHALL NOT show it.

THE tree view SHALL make each row's hit area the tree's whole width, however far its content and its container are set in (TRV-3), and the row's whole height, with no gap between the hit areas of two rows. WHERE input is touch, or the platform cannot tell the input type, a row SHALL be at least sys.target.touch high, drawn so, in both densities, because rows that touch cannot extend a hit area over each other; for a fine pointer a row SHALL be at least sys.target.pointer high WHILE density is regular, and WHILE density is compact as high as its density gives, the one place where a row of the tree is lower than the pointer target. In the row of a parent that can be chosen, the chevron's own hit area SHALL be, WHILE chevron is start, the part of the row's hit area from its start edge to the middle of the gap after the chevron's box, and WHILE chevron is end, the part from the middle of the gap before the chevron's box to the row's end edge; WHILE chevron is none, the icon's hit area of TRV-44 is the part from the row's start edge to the middle of the gap after the icon. Each SHALL be at least sys.target.touch wide for touch and sys.target.pointer wide for a fine pointer, reaching over what stands beside the mark where the box gives less.
behavior.verify: Under the default system: a regular row is 48 high for every input; a compact row is 32 high for a mouse and 48 for touch. Test that a press at the tree's start edge beside a row of the third level is a press on that row's chevron, and that with chevron end a press at the row's end edge is.

behavior.text: WHILE an item's disabled is true THE tree view SHALL render its container, label, supporting text, trailing text, icon, chevron and opacity from the disabled component tokens of its condition, and SHALL apply that opacity to the whole row, its trailing content included, and to nothing else: the focus ring of TRV-25 SHALL be drawn at full strength on a disabled row that has keyboard focus, because the arrow keys reach it and the ring says where focus is; SHALL NOT emit change or toggle for a press, a key or a touch on it; SHALL draw no hover and no press answer on it; and SHALL expose it as disabled. The arrow keys SHALL still reach it, so that people learn it exists. The item SHALL keep its place, its selection and its open: a disabled parent that is open still shows the items it holds, which keep their own disabled, and the product MAY still set its open and select it. A row that draws no fill at rest SHALL draw none while disabled.
behavior.verify: The fixture disabled: the closed parent "generated" is disabled and cannot be opened; the open parent "themes" is disabled and its two items can still be chosen.

behavior.text: WHEN an item's row is pressed by pointer, touch, Enter or Space THE tree view SHALL show its pressed state without delay and SHALL keep it visible for at least sys.motion.duration.press-hold, even when the press ends sooner.

WHILE an item's row is pressed THE tree view SHALL answer as sys.behavior.pressed-feedback names: overlay applies the pressed tokens to the whole container at once; ripple grows the pressed state layer, clipped to the container (indented or full as highlight says), from the point of contact (from the center for keyboard activation); dim applies the pressed opacity to the whole row and draws no state layer; none draws no answer to the press. Under ripple and dim only the container color stays with the state under the press; label, supporting text, trailing text, icon, chevron and opacity still come from the pressed tokens. Under none every part stays with the state under the press. The ripple grows over comp.tree-view.motion.feedback-duration with comp.tree-view.motion.state-easing, fades over comp.tree-view.motion.state-duration with comp.tree-view.motion.state-easing once the press has ended and press-hold has passed, and appears whole where motion is reduced.
behavior.verify: Test under a system that sets each value; `m3-like` is ripple, `cupertino` is dim, the default is overlay.

behavior.text: THE tree view SHALL ease its rows' container corners by sys.shape.corner-smoothing (0 is a quarter circle, 0.6 the iOS continuous corner; a platform with only the OS curve draws it for any amount above 0) and show a row's keyboard focus as sys.behavior.focus-style names (ring or glow); a platform that cannot draw a choice SHALL fall back to the first value and state that in its README.
behavior.verify: `cupertino` is continuous; the `acme` fixture system is glow.

behavior.text: WHEN the colors of a row change between states, or between the unselected and the selected condition, THE tree view SHALL animate them over comp.tree-view.motion.state-duration with comp.tree-view.motion.state-easing, and SHALL change them at once where motion is reduced. The selected fill SHALL NOT slide from one row to another.

THE tree view SHALL expose itself as a tree named by label, and as one in which several items may be selected WHILE selection is multiple; each item as one tree item named by its label (the text of the label slot's content where the product gave one), described by its supporting text, then the text of its trailing content, then its trailing text, with its level, its place among the items of its parent and their number; a parent with its expanded or collapsed state WHILE the tree is expandable, and with none WHILE it is not (TRV-49), and the items it shows as a group that belongs to it in either case; WHILE selection is single or multiple, each item that can be chosen with its selected state, true or false, and an item that cannot with none; a disabled item as disabled and a loading parent as busy; and the chevron, the icon and the guide lines hidden. WHILE a name is being edited the edit field SHALL be exposed as a text field inside the row it stands in, named by editLabel, and keyboard focus SHALL be in it; a new row (TRV-48) SHALL be exposed as a tree item at its level holding that field. WHILE editLabel is empty and a field is open THE tree view SHALL still open the field, and in debug builds report that it has no name. On the web these are the tree, treeitem and group roles with aria-expanded, aria-selected, aria-multiselectable, aria-disabled and aria-busy, the level, the set size and the position coming from the nesting of the elements. WHERE a platform has no tree semantics THE tree view SHALL expose each row as one element in the order drawn, with that name and description, the expanded or collapsed state, the selected state and the disabled state as the platform says them, and its level by the platform's own means where it has one; it SHALL NOT invent words for a level, and the platform's README SHALL say what a person is not told. WHILE label is empty THE tree view SHALL still render, and in debug builds report that the tree has no accessible name; WHILE an item's label is empty and its label slot holds nothing it SHALL report that the item has none.
behavior.verify: On the web: the fixture single has one element with the tree role named "Project files"; every row is a treeitem; parents carry aria-expanded and leaves do not; exactly one treeitem has aria-selected true and every other one that has a value has it false; no row holds a second focusable element.

behavior.text: WHEN a parent opens or closes, and WHEN the selection changes, THE tree view SHALL let the changed state of the row be the only thing assistive technology is told: it SHALL announce nothing itself, SHALL have no live region, and SHALL NOT move keyboard or screen-reader focus, except as TRV-12 says for a row that goes away and TRV-45 to TRV-48 say for an edit field.

WHILE the text size is enlarged THE tree view SHALL grow its labels, its supporting texts and its trailing texts with it, keep its paddings, gaps and indents, and grow each row in height; a label and a supporting text on one line (TRV-6, TRV-7) SHALL be cut with an ellipsis and shown whole in the tooltip of TRV-50, and with labelWrap and supportingWrap they SHALL wrap and the rows grow; it SHALL keep the chevron's and the icon's boxes at their token sizes, both still centred on the label's first line (TRV-2), SHALL set no fixed height, SHALL lose no content when the reader raises line height, paragraph spacing, letter spacing or word spacing (a one-line text is cut, and is whole in its tooltip and its accessible name), and SHALL need no horizontal scrolling at a width of 320 points with text at 200 %, where TRV-3 keeps half of the width for names.
behavior.verify: Test the fixtures long-labels-wrap and deep at 200 % text in a stage 320 wide: every character of every label is visible, each chevron is on its row's first line, and nothing overlaps; in long-labels each cut label is whole in its tooltip.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform draws with a person's own forced colors (the web's forced-colors mode, and a platform's equivalent where it has one) THE tree view SHALL draw its labels, texts, icons and chevrons in the platform's text color; the guide lines in that text color; a selected row in the platform's colors for a selected item, fill and text, and in addition with an edge in the text color inside its container, because the mode may remove a fill; a disabled row in the platform's color for disabled text; and a row's hover, press and focus in the platform's own colors, with the focus ring still inside the row. Open and closed SHALL still be told apart by the chevron's turn, which no color carries.
behavior.verify: On the web, with forced colors emulated: the fixture single draws its selected row in Highlight and HighlightText with an edge; the fixture guides draws its lines in CanvasText; the fixture disabled draws its disabled rows in GrayText.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left THE tree view SHALL mirror a row and apply its paddings and its indent by logical start and end: the tree's start edge is its right edge, each level begins further to the left, the chevron's box at the start is at the right of its row with the icon, the text, the trailing content, the trailing text and an end chevron after it toward the left, and the guide lines stand under the parents' first leading things. A closed parent's start chevron SHALL point to the left, drawn so by the icon helper, which mirrors the glyph because the icon set marks chevron_right (TRV-38), and an open parent's SHALL point down. The arrow keys of TRV-21 SHALL follow the direction: Left opens and steps in, Right closes and steps out; Up, Down, Home and End SHALL be the same in both directions. A ripple SHALL still grow from the point of contact.
behavior.verify: The fixtures rtl and rtl-guides-compact: the indent grows from the right edge, closed chevrons point left, open ones down.

behavior.text: THE tree view SHALL take its layout direction from where it is used — the direction of the nearest ancestor that sets one, and the platform's own where none does — and SHALL have no direction setting of its own; WHEN that direction changes while the tree view is shown THE tree view SHALL draw itself for the new direction at once, without a motion of its own, keeping its selection, every parent's open and its focus.
behavior.verify: Test with the direction set on an ancestor inside the page or the view tree, not on the root, and again changed after the first render.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left THE tree view SHALL draw an item's icon and a parent's chevron mirrored left to right exactly when the system's icon set marks that glyph's name as mirrored or the product forces mirroring for that use, and unmirrored when the product forbids it: the icon helper mirrors the glyph inside its own box, about the box's vertical centre line, changing neither its place, size, color and fill nor the order TRV-2 gives. THE tree view SHALL NOT mirror a glyph itself, and SHALL NOT mirror content the product gives as an image or a view of its own rather than by a glyph's name. The quarter turn of an open parent's chevron (TRV-4) is the tree's and SHALL end pointing down in both directions.
behavior.verify: chevron_right and arrow_forward are marked by the default icon set; folder and settings are not. The fixture icons-rtl draws arrow_forward mirrored and folder and settings unmirrored.

behavior.text: THE tree view SHALL lay out an item's label, its supporting text and its trailing text, and the words of a loading row, each as text of its own direction, isolated from the text around it: each takes the base direction of its first strong character, or the layout direction where it has none, so that a left-to-right file name, a path, a number with its unit and a version keep their own order in a right-to-left layout and reorder nothing beside them; THE tree view SHALL still place each and align its lines by the layout direction, not by the text's own, and SHALL cut a trailing text that does not fit (TRV-7) at the end of its own direction.
behavior.verify: The fixture ltr-labels-rtl draws left-to-right file names in a right-to-left stage: each name begins at the right of its text column and reads left to right, a trailing "/" stays at the name's right end, and the chevrons are at the right.

behavior.text: WHILE the system's icon set cannot yet draw a glyph of the tree view (its font is still loading) THE tree view SHALL draw nothing in that glyph's place, never the glyph's name as text, SHALL keep the glyph's box, and SHALL draw the glyph once the set can; a parent SHALL open and close all the same.

WHEN density names a value that the active design system does not have THE tree view SHALL render with the default density's tokens, and WHEN selection names a value the tree view does not define it SHALL render with none, WHEN chevron names one it SHALL render as start, WHEN guides names one as none, WHEN highlight names one as indented and WHEN iconSpace names one as auto; WHEN indent, iconGap or stickyMax is not a number of zero or more it SHALL render as its default; in debug builds it SHALL report the unknown value. WHEN selection changes while the tree is shown THE tree view SHALL draw the new form at once, keeping every parent's open and its focus, and SHALL emit no change for it.

IF the tree view has no items THE tree view SHALL draw nothing, take no space, expose nothing and be no stop in the focus order: the words for an empty hierarchy are the product's, beside the tree. IF an item holds no items and its expandable is false THE tree view SHALL treat it as a leaf whatever its open and loading say. WHEN items are added to or removed from a shown tree THE tree view SHALL draw them at once, without the motion of TRV-11, keeping the selection, every other parent's open and, as far as TRV-12 allows, its focus.

THE tree view SHALL keep the room of an icon (comp.tree-view.icon.size.regular for regular and comp.tree-view.icon.size.compact for compact, and iconGap after it) in the row of an item whose icon is empty WHILE iconSpace is always, and WHILE iconSpace is auto and another item of the same level — the items of the same parent, or of the first level — has an icon, so that the labels of a level stand in one column; WHILE iconSpace is never, and WHILE it is auto and no item of the level has an icon, it SHALL keep no such room. The kept room SHALL draw nothing and SHALL count as the icon's for the step of TRV-3 and for the guides of TRV-8 only as room: a guide stands under an icon that is drawn, and under the label's start where the room is empty.
behavior.verify: The fixture icon-space-auto (one level with an icon on some rows, one level with none): in the first the labels stand in one column, in the second the labels begin where an icon would be. The fixture icon-space-never: each label begins after its own icon, or where the icon would be where it has none. Test always on a tree with no icons: every label begins an icon and a gap in.

behavior.text: WHILE chevron is none THE tree view SHALL draw no chevron and keep no chevron's box, and SHALL open and close a parent that is not disabled as follows. By the keyboard, the arrows of TRV-21 SHALL always open and close it, whether or not it can be chosen. By pointer or touch: WHERE the parent's row has an icon, a press on the icon SHALL open or close it, emit its toggle once and never choose, its hit area being TRV-26's; WHERE it has no icon and cannot be chosen, a press anywhere on its row SHALL open or close it (TRV-10); WHERE it has no icon and can be chosen, a press on its row SHALL choose it (TRV-16, TRV-17) and SHALL NOT open or close it — selection wins, and the keyboard still opens it. A parent that names an icon and an open icon shows open and closed by its glyph (TRV-5); a parent with neither shows it by the expanded state alone, which assistive technology is told (TRV-32), and in debug builds THE tree view SHALL report a parent that has no icon and no open icon once, because nothing on screen shows whether it is open.
behavior.verify: The fixture chevron-none (selection single): no row keeps a chevron's box; a press on a closed parent's icon emits one toggle and no change, and a press on its label one change and no toggle; Right Arrow opens it. Test in a tree with chevron none and parents without icons: a press on the row of a parent without a value opens it; on one with a value, chooses it and opens nothing; a debug build reports each parent without an icon.

behavior.text: WHILE editable is true THE tree view SHALL open an edit field on an item's name (TRV-46) WHEN the user double-clicks or double-taps the label of its row, WHEN the user presses F2 while keyboard focus is on its row, and WHEN the product asks the tree view to edit that item (the platform's method for it). It SHALL NOT open one on a disabled item, on the loading row, or on an item whose label is given by content of the label slot rather than by plain text, whose inline content is the product's to edit; and WHILE editable is false it SHALL open none, leaving F2 and a double-click to the platform and doing nothing when asked. The two presses of a double-click SHALL each be answered as TRV-10 to TRV-17 say, and the field SHALL open after the second. Only one field SHALL be open in a tree at a time: opening one, by any of these means or by TRV-48, SHALL first commit the one that is open.
behavior.verify: Test in a tree whose editable is true: a double-click on a leaf's label, F2 on a focused row and the platform's method each open the field; F2 on a disabled item opens none; in a tree whose editable is false none of the three opens one.

behavior.text: WHILE an edit field is open on an item THE tree view SHALL draw an Embedded text input component of one line over the item's label, in the box of the label's first line — the same font, line height, start and width, so that opening and closing the field moves nothing in the row or beside it — in the label's text style and color, the label and a supporting text inline after it not drawn under it, holding the label, with keyboard focus in it and — for a leaf whose label holds a dot after its first character — the text before the last dot selected, and for any other item the whole label selected; and SHALL draw around the field's box the focus indicator of TRV-25 (sys.behavior.focus-style), inside the row, while the chevron or its box, the icon, the trailing content, the trailing text, the row's selection and the row's open stay as they were. The row SHALL keep at least its height, and a long name SHALL scroll inside the field rather than widen the tree. Every key typed in the field SHALL be the field's: WHEN the user presses Enter, or WHEN focus leaves the field by any other means (Tab, a press elsewhere, the window losing focus), THE tree view SHALL commit the field; WHEN the user presses Escape it SHALL close the field without emitting; WHILE an input method is composing Enter and Escape SHALL be the input method's. WHEN the field commits THE tree view SHALL close it and, WHERE its text with white space removed at both ends is not empty and differs from the label, emit the item's rename exactly once with that text and the label it had; otherwise it SHALL close the field without emitting. THE tree view SHALL NOT change the label itself: it SHALL draw the label it had until the product sets the new one. WHEN the field closes on Enter or Escape keyboard focus SHALL return to the item's row; WHEN it closes because focus left it, focus SHALL stay where it went. WHILE the field is open THE tree view SHALL NOT answer a press inside it as a press on the row (TRV-10), and WHEN the item is removed, becomes disabled, or is hidden because a parent above it closes, or editable becomes false, it SHALL close the field without emitting.
behavior.verify: Test: in a field opened on button.ts, the text before the extension is selected, and the row, its neighbours and the field's text stand where the row and its label stood (to a pixel), open and closed; typing a name and Enter emits one rename with the new label and the label it had, keeps the old label drawn, and puts focus back on the row; Escape emits nothing; a name of white space only emits nothing; pressing elsewhere commits.

behavior.text: WHILE an edit field is open on an item THE tree view SHALL keep that item where it is and keep its row's state of selection, open, hover and press as they were; SHALL take none of the keys of TRV-20 to TRV-23 from the field; and SHALL change nothing about the selection or about any parent's open because a field opened, committed or closed. WHEN the product sets the item's label in answer to rename THE tree view SHALL draw it at once, without a motion of its own (the label of a row is the product's, TRV-6).
behavior.verify: Test: arrow keys and type-ahead in an open field move the caret and the text, not the tree's focus; committing emits no change and no toggle; a label the product sets in answer to rename is drawn in the same frame.

WHEN its field commits with a text that, with white space removed at both ends, is not empty THE tree view SHALL take the new row away and emit create exactly once with that text, whether it is a parent, the item it goes under (none at the first level) and the item it follows (none where it is first); WHEN the product adds an item in the new row's place in answer, before the next frame is drawn, focus SHALL move to that item's row. WHEN the field closes on Escape or commits empty THE tree view SHALL take the new row away, emit nothing, and return focus to the row that had it. Escape takes the row away and emits nothing. In a tree with no selection and no focus the new row is the last of the first level.

behavior.text: WHILE expandable is false THE tree view SHALL draw every parent as open whatever its open says, draw no chevron and keep no chevron's box, emit no toggle, open and close nothing for a press, a key or the platform's search, and expose no parent as expanded or collapsed: each item is a tree item at its level, a parent's items a group that belongs to it (the tree pattern's tree items without the expanded state are end nodes to a screen reader, and their groups still tell the level). The arrow toward the end of the line SHALL move focus to a parent's first item and the one toward the start to an item's parent (TRV-21), and the asterisk SHALL do nothing. A press on a row SHALL choose an item that can be chosen and do nothing on any other. An item's own expandable SHALL be read only WHILE the tree's expandable is true. WHEN expandable becomes true the tree SHALL draw each parent as its open says, at once.

It SHALL hold the label alone WHERE the item has no supporting text, and the label as the title and the supporting text as the text of a rich tooltip WHERE it has one. WHILE nothing of the row is cut THE tree view SHALL show no tooltip for it. The tooltip SHALL be hidden from assistive technology, which is given the whole label as the row's name and the whole supporting text as its description (TRV-32); no touch long-press opens it, because a long-press on a row is the platform's.
behavior.verify: Test in the fixture long-labels: hovering a cut label shows the tooltip with the whole label after the show delay; Escape hides it; keyboard focus on the row shows it at once; hovering a label that fits shows none.

behavior.text: WHILE highlight is indented THE tree view SHALL draw a row's container — its fill (selected or of a state), its state layer and ripple, and its focus indicator — from where the row's content's level begins, less the row's padding, to the tree's end edge; WHILE highlight is full it SHALL draw them from the tree's start edge to its end edge whatever the row's level, the content still beginning one step further in for each level (TRV-3). The corners (comp.tree-view.container.shape) and the focus ring follow the container in both.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is multiple THE tree view SHALL answer, besides TRV-17, the keys and presses of the tree pattern's multi-select model, each emitting change exactly once where values changed and never opening or closing anything: Shift with Down Arrow or Up Arrow SHALL move focus to the next or previous row shown and select every item that can be chosen from the anchor to the focused row, deselecting the items of the range it selected before that are no longer in it, and leaving every other value as it was; Shift with Space SHALL do the same from the anchor to the focused row without moving focus; Ctrl (Command on Apple platforms) with Shift and Home or End SHALL select every item that can be chosen from the focused row to the first or the last row shown and move focus there; Ctrl (Command) with A SHALL select every item that can be chosen among the rows shown; a press with Shift SHALL select from the anchor to the pressed row as Shift with Space does; a press with Ctrl (Command) SHALL toggle the pressed item as a plain press does (TRV-17). The anchor SHALL be the item last chosen or unchosen by a plain press, a press with Ctrl (Command), Space or Enter, and where there is none the focused row. Items that cannot be chosen (no value, disabled) SHALL be passed over in a range and keep their state. WHILE selection is single or none these keys and modifiers SHALL be the platform's, except that a press with a modifier SHALL do what a plain press does.

behavior.text: WHILE stickyParents is true and stickyMax is more than 0, and the tree stands in a scrolling box, THE tree view SHALL pin at the top of that box the rows of the open parents that hold the topmost row shown below the pinned rows, one per level in the order of their levels, the innermost stickyMax of them where more parents are open above it, each held in place while what it holds scrolls under it and leaving with its last row; it SHALL pin the rows themselves — the same rows, with their own fill, state, selection, focus, press and the events of a press, never a copy in the accessibility tree — drawn over the rows that scroll under them with comp.tree-view.sticky.container.color under their own fill and a line comp.tree-view.sticky.divider.width wide in comp.tree-view.sticky.divider.color under the last of them. WHEN keyboard focus moves onto a row that lies under the pinned rows THE tree view SHALL have the scrolling box bring that row into view below them by the least distance. A guide line SHALL pass under a pinned row (TRV-8). Nothing about pinning SHALL move by itself: there is no motion to reduce. A tree that stands in no scrolling box of its own, or whose stickyParents is false, SHALL pin nothing. A platform whose scrolling list cannot hold a row in place SHALL draw the pinned rows as an overlay hidden from assistive technology that keeps focus on the real rows, and SHALL say so in its README.
behavior.verify: Test the fixture deep in a scrolling box 200 high: scrolled so that the fifth level's rows are at the top, the rows of the third and the fourth level's parents (stickyMax 2) are pinned at the top, one row high each, and the second level's is not; with stickyMax 3 the second's is pinned too; pressing a pinned parent's chevron closes it; Down Arrow onto a row under the pinned rows scrolls it below them; with stickyParents false nothing is pinned.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has ARIA attributes (the web), the host carries its tree role (TRV-32) itself, so what the product writes on it is not moved, but for a name: WHILE label is not empty THE tree view SHALL hold the product's aria-label and aria-labelledby on that host as their data-aria- twins, so that label is its whole name although the platform gives aria-labelledby the precedence, and WHEN label is emptied SHALL give them back as they were written; WHILE label is empty a name the product gives so — aria-label, or aria-labelledby naming an element — SHALL be its name and SHALL NOT be reported as having none in debug builds (TRV-32). WHEN the product removes one, or its data-aria- twin, or sets the ARIA property that reflects it (ariaLabel, ariaLabelledByElements) to null, THE tree view SHALL take it away.

Moves focus to the first or the last row that is shown.

What a press on the row does: chooses the item where it can be chosen (single: selects it; multiple: adds it to or removes it from the selection); opens or closes a parent that cannot be chosen; nothing on a leaf that cannot be chosen.
Opens every closed parent among the focused row's siblings. Focus stays.
Moves focus to the next shown row whose label begins with the characters typed.
